## [0.7.0] - 2026-09-13

### Added

- The `app` container now shuts down gracefully on `docker stop`/`docker compose down` instead of terminating immediately: it stops accepting new requests, lets in-flight ones (including open Reports/check-in live-update streams) finish for up to 6 seconds before forcing them closed, then gives the database disconnect up to 3 more seconds - 9 seconds combined, comfortably inside Docker's default 10-second stop window, so a routine restart or host maintenance no longer risks cutting off a request that was already in progress. The background worker container already did this; this closes the same gap for the web server.
- Organisation Settings has a new **Notifications** tab for security alerts to admin staff, split across three cards: **Webhook** (Discord, Slack, or generic JSON destination, with its own **Send test** next to Payload format reporting the webhook and in-app results), **Email** (a table of extra recipients who get every enabled alert regardless of their own personal opt-out - each with an optional description, a write-time "added at/by" stamp, and its own Send test/Edit/Remove actions, Remove behind a confirmation step), and **Notification types**, a grid with one row per foundation alert type (repeated failed logins, emergency two-factor bypass use, login or security settings changed, admin login from a new country) and an independent on/off switch per channel (webhook, email, in-app) - so a single alert type can be routed to some channels and not others. Turning a channel off for a type only stops active delivery on that channel; the underlying security event is still recorded either way.
- Repeated failed sign-in attempts on an admin account, use of the emergency two-factor bypass, changes to organisation login or security settings (single sign-on provider or Cloudflare Access), and an admin account signing in from a country not seen among its recent successful logins now all actually trigger the alert configured in Organisation Settings → Notifications, on top of the audit trail these already wrote before.
- Organisation Settings → Notifications and My Account's own Notifications section now describe each alert type in plain language instead of technical shorthand ("MFA" reads as "two-factor authentication", "SSO" as "single sign-on", "brute-force" and "credential-stuffing" are explained in a sentence instead of named) - both the on-screen grid and the actual alert emails now use the same wording. My Account's grid also gained the same one-line description already shown in Organisation Settings' grid, which it was previously missing, and each grid's severity icon is now vertically centered against its type's full two-line label instead of only its first line.
- My Account has a new **Notifications** section where each admin controls their own Email and In-app delivery per alert type, independent of what other admins receive - the shared team webhook stays organisation-wide and isn't personalized here. A new bell in the topbar shows an unread count that updates automatically, and opens a short list of recent alerts (across every organisation the account has access to, each one labeled with which organisation it's from) where clicking an unread one marks it read, or "Mark all as read" clears the whole list at once.
- Communication's Email/Templates preview now has a Light/Dark toggle next to the mock inbox so admins can check how a ticket email will render in a dark-mode mail client before sending - Dark switches the mock inbox chrome to a dark theme and darkens the previewed message body itself (backgrounds and text, matched to the neighborhood of real dark-mode surfaces like Gmail/Outlook/Apple Mail rather than pure black), while logos, QR codes, hero images, and wallet badges keep their original colors so they stay recognizable.
- Attendees' Filters panel now lets you pick several ticket types, attendance statuses, or mail delivery statuses at once instead of only one at a time (for example "VIP or Staff" rather than one ticket type per look), on both the on-screen list and CSV/XLSX/PDF exports.
- The notification bell's dropdown now has a trash icon to permanently clear your own notification history at once (asks for confirmation first), next to the existing "mark all as read" checkmark icon - only your organisation's underlying security audit trail is unaffected, and future alerts still arrive normally afterward. Anything never cleared is now also automatically deleted after 30 days by the background worker, configurable via `NOTIFICATION_RETENTION_DAYS`, the same retention pattern already used for the security audit log.
- Attendees' Filters panel can now also filter by any custom attendee field defined on the event's Requirements page (for example T-Shirt size or Networking & Dinner) - a multi-select for choice fields, an Any/Yes/No toggle for yes/no fields, and a contains-text search for free-text fields - on both the on-screen list and CSV/XLSX/PDF exports, the same as the four built-in filters.

### Changed

- My Account is now organized into four tabs - **Profile**, **Password** (including two-factor authentication), **Sessions**, and **Notifications** - instead of one long scrolling page. The active tab is reflected in the URL (`?tab=`), so a reload or a bookmarked link returns to the same section; nothing about what each section shows or does has changed. Active sessions are now paginated (10 per page by default, adjustable), and on phone-width screens the list switches from a table to a stacked card per session - the same responsive pattern Users & roles' own Active sessions tab already uses - instead of forcing horizontal scrolling.
- Organisation Settings → Branding's Theme card no longer has a separate "Primary colour" picker: it's merged into a renamed **Theme by surface** section, where Admin panel, Registration form, and Ticket page each get their own colour control right next to their existing font control. Admin panel's colour is now the instance's base colour; Ticket page can pick its own accent colour or keep inheriting Admin panel's ("Same as Admin panel"), the same choice it already had for its font. Registration form's colour control stays disabled, matching its font control, since that surface doesn't exist yet.
- My Account's passkey management now sends a best-effort WebAuthn Signal API notification when removing a passkey or security key. Supported browsers and password managers can then stop offering the deleted credential for future sign-ins. The "Add" button for passkeys is also now disabled on browsers that report no passkey support, instead of only failing after the setup prompt is attempted.
- Reports' Wallets tab time-to-install charts ("Time to wallet install" and "Time to install after reminder", both in the live tab and the printable/exportable report) now label their fastest bucket "Within 24h" instead of "Same day" - the bucket has always meant "installed within a day of the email", not "the same calendar date", and an install that happened the next morning could still land there, which the old label made look like a mismatch.
- Security notification emails (repeated failed logins, emergency two-factor bypass use, etc.) now share the same visual construction as the mail transport test email - white card, header logo, footer - instead of a separately-designed template, so a recipient has the same visual cue that it genuinely came from their own Admitto instance. Their subject line now starts with the organisation's name instead of "[Admitto]", since a self-hosted instance's own admins already know it's Admitto sending; what they need at a glance is which organisation the alert concerns. The team Discord webhook for the same alerts is more readable too: fields render one per line instead of Discord's cramped 3-per-row layout, metadata keys are shown in plain words instead of raw field names, the alert's time appears in the embed, and the title carries a severity icon.
- Reports' Mail tab **Attendee reach** card, and its printable PDF summary, now split the previous single "Not reached" count into **Never sent** (no email attempt was ever made) and **Send failed** (at least one attempt was made, but every one of them failed to deliver) - "Not reached" alone read as if the email had failed to arrive, which wasn't accurate for attendees who were simply never sent one in the first place. The exported CSV already lists each attendee's own delivery attempts and last delivery status, so it needed no change.
- Communication's Templates tab MJML/HTML body field is now a real code editor (CodeMirror) instead of a plain text box - line numbers, syntax highlighting, and bracket matching, with the same placeholder-chip-at-cursor insertion, Tab-to-indent, and drag-to-resize behavior as the old textarea. `{{placeholder}}` tokens (e.g. `{{first_name}}`, `{{logo_url}}`) are also visually marked with a subtle info-tint highlight wherever they appear - in body text or inside an attribute value - so they stand out from the surrounding static markup. An unrecognized `{{typo}}` now gets a red underline and gutter marker right where it is, live as you type, instead of only surfacing as a list of errors below the editor after Save or Preview. Typing `{{` also now offers the template's own placeholders as an autocomplete list (with the same description shown on the chip tooltips), so inserting one no longer requires reaching for a chip above the editor - picking one no longer produces duplicate closing braces (auto-close-brackets was already inserting its own before the pick landed), and typing `{{` no longer momentarily sends an invalid empty placeholder to the live preview. Selecting text that includes a `{{placeholder}}` token now visibly shows the selection instead of the placeholder's own highlight hiding it, and the autocomplete popup stays clear of the screen edge on narrow phones instead of touching it. Code folding and search (Ctrl+F) were already available for free and just weren't discoverable.

### Fixed

- The notification bell's unread badge could show a higher number than the dropdown's own list could ever display or let you mark as read - the badge counted every unread notification, while the list itself only ever shows the most recent 30. The badge now caps at the same 30, so it always matches what you can actually see and act on.
- The confirmation dialog (used across the app for destructive actions, most recently the notification bell's "Clear all") rendered behind - not in front of - any already-open dropdown panel, since it had its own hardcoded stacking order instead of using the shared elevation scale every other overlay follows. It now sits correctly on top of everything, including a dropdown it was opened from.
- Security alerts from Organisation Settings → Notifications (repeated failed logins, emergency two-factor bypass use, settings changed, new-country logins) named the affected account with a masked, partially garbled identifier (for example "a*** at example.com") instead of a real name or email - the account is now shown by its display name where known, otherwise its real email. Settings-change alerts also now name the specific thing that changed (for example a single sign-on provider's own configured name) instead of only its internal database id, which had no way to be looked up from the admin UI.
- System logs' `mail_sent` entries for a security alert now show the real recipient address instead of a masked one, for any recipient who is a verified Admitto staff account (already fully visible elsewhere in the admin panel) - masking added no real privacy protection there, only made it harder to confirm an alert reached the right person. An organisation's extra email recipients and the address used by "Send test" stay masked, same as any other mail, since those can be any address an admin typed in rather than a real staff account.
- The optional Redis-backed cross-process live-update fan-out (used only when `REDIS_URL` is configured, so the background worker's own mail-drain/import-drain activity can reach the admin app's live streams; ADR 0044) could very rarely deliver the same event twice to a process's own subscribers - if the Redis PUBLISH command's reply arrived after the client gave up waiting for it, that timeout was mistaken for the command never having reached Redis at all, triggering a redundant local delivery on top of the one already arriving through the normal subscription. It now only falls back to a direct local delivery when the connection genuinely failed, not merely when it timed out waiting for a reply that may still be on its way.
- A large batch of error and warning messages across the admin app (Add attendee, Edit attendee, Create event, delivery details, sent-message preview, mail settings, external services, the setup wizard, and several other screens) now render as the same bordered notice box used everywhere else, instead of plain unstyled or ad-hoc colored text - the "This email is already registered for this event." message was one of several places still on the older pattern. A few pages that could previously fail to load with no way to recover (the check-in event picker, the Communication template editor, a wizard mail-settings step) now show a clear message with a Retry action instead of leaving the screen blank or relying on a toast that disappears. Several messages describing the same underlying failure in different words across screens (for example "Couldn't load X" vs "Could not load X") were also made consistent, and a few messages that stated a problem without suggesting a fix now do.
- Requirements' load-error screen previously kept the generic "Could not load requirements" heading even when the real cause was a permission failure, right next to a description explaining that specific cause - it now titles that case "You do not have access to this event" instead, matching the same fix already applied to the Communication template editor.
- Communication's Templates tab had two small visual inconsistencies in the template editor: the "Subject" field sat flush against the wallet-chips notice above it with no breathing room, and the "MJML body"/"HTML body" label rendered in a different color and weight than every other field label on the page (including "Subject" right above it) because it used its own hand-rolled styling instead of the shared label component.
- Outbound mail sends through the Microsoft Graph and Power Automate transports now have the same 15-second timeout their own connection probes and Graph's token request already had, closing a gap where a provider that accepted the connection and then never responded could hang the send indefinitely instead of failing over to a retry; Power Automate's pre-send DNS-rebinding recheck is now bounded by the same deadline for the same reason.
- The "Send test email" message (Mail transport settings) no longer shows a broken-image icon in classic desktop Outlook when no organisation or event logo is set - it fell back to the Admitto wordmark as an SVG, which that client's rendering engine cannot display as an `<img>`; it now falls back to a bundled PNG instead. The same message could also render with an inverted (near-black) background in mail clients that auto-remap colors for dark mode (Outlook.com, Apple Mail); it now explicitly opts out, matching how a real, production ticket email already does.
- Expanding the tablet-width (768-1279px) sidebar rail from its collapsed icon-only state showed only the Admitto mark, not the full wordmark next to it, even though the expanded rail is exactly as wide as the desktop sidebar where the wordmark always shows - the rule hiding the wordmark for that width range never checked whether the rail was actually collapsed or expanded, unlike every other rule in that same responsive block.
- That same tablet-rail expand/collapse animates its width rather than snapping instantly, but the wordmark and the "ADMINISTRATION" section label only show or hide via an instant class change, so for the brief duration of that animation they rendered at their full resting size before the rail had actually widened enough to fit them, spilling past its edge into the page content next to it. The sidebar now clips its own contents horizontally, so anything not yet fits during the animation is cleanly cropped instead of overflowing.

- Text inputs with a leading icon (the Attendees search box, Event settings' "Event link ID" field, and every other field built the same way) rendered about 12.5% narrower than their siblings on phones and tablets, clipping placeholder text and typed values mid-word with no ellipsis - the CSS rule that inflates an input's width before scaling it back down (packages/ui's `pointer: coarse` fix for iOS Safari's input-focus zoom) let the input's flex container shrink it back to size before the scale-down ran, so the later shrink was applied twice. Plain inputs without a leading icon were unaffected.
- Those same leading-icon fields also lost their top border on phones and tablets (for example Add attendee's Email/First name/Last name/Company/Department fields and the Attendees search box) - the same `pointer: coarse` scaling trick centers the field vertically before shrinking it, but was scaling down from its top edge instead of its center, leaving the shrunk field floating a couple of pixels above where it should sit so its top border landed outside the field's clipping box and disappeared.
- The icon inside those same fields was invisible on phones and tablets too, for an unrelated reason: the scaling trick's `transform` on the input creates a new stacking context, which - combined with the input's own opaque background and sitting later in the markup than the icon - painted the input over the top of the icon instead of the other way around. The icon now has an explicit vertical center (independent of the field's own layout) and a higher stacking order so it stays on top and stays put.

### Security

- Adding or re-discovering a single sign-on provider now verifies that the identity provider's own discovery document reports the exact issuer that was configured, matching OWASP ASVS V10.5.3 - previously Admitto stored whichever issuer the fetched document claimed, without checking it against the URL actually configured, and that stored value is what every future sign-in token is verified against.
- Creating a custom attendee field (Requirements page) now rejects `__proto__`, `constructor`, and `prototype` as its internal identifier, alongside the existing reserved names already rejected for colliding with a built-in profile column - the slug format already allowed all three, and a field named one of them could crash the Attendees list for every admin viewing that event, since its per-field filter state looks values up by that same identifier on a plain object.
- A successful attendees export job's own retained metadata (`AdminJob.result_json`) no longer keeps a custom text field's raw filter value verbatim (for example a dietary-notes search term) - it only recorded a "was this filter used" presence flag when the export failed or was reclaimed as stale, not when it completed normally, which was by far the more common outcome.
- Every admin account now gets a personal, non-dismissible notification (email and in-app, via My Account's own Notifications section) whenever its password, two-factor method, passkey, trusted devices, or single sign-on connection changes, whether they made the change themselves or another admin made it for them - so an unauthorized change to your own account is never silent, matching OWASP ASVS V6.3.7. Unlike every other alert type, this one cannot be turned off by the account owner or the organisation, since the whole point is to survive an attacker who already has access trying to silence it. This now also covers every remaining way a credential can change: an administrator resetting another admin's two-factor or password, unlinking their single sign-on connection, a forced password change on first login, and linking a new single sign-on connection to an already-signed-in account.
- Admin accounts now also get a personal notification when their own account signs in from a country not seen among its recent successful logins, matching OWASP ASVS V6.3.5 - previously only the rest of the admin team was told about this, never the account whose credentials might actually be compromised. Same as the notification above, this one can't be turned off, for the same reason. The account owner no longer also receives a duplicate copy of the org-wide alert meant for the rest of the admin team - they only get their own personal one.
- The rest of the admin team is now notified (via Organisation Settings → Notifications, same as the other security alerts) whenever a user is granted the admin or superadmin role, matching NIST SP 800-53 AC-2(1) - previously a role change of this kind left no alert at all, only the existing audit trail. This also covers a role gained automatically through a single sign-on or Cloudflare Access group mapping, not just a grant made directly in Users and roles - arguably the more important case, since nobody is watching an identity provider's own group membership change the way an admin action is seen as it happens. A same-or-lower-rank role change, such as moving a superadmin down to admin, is a demotion and correctly does not trigger this alert. When the grant is for a specific organisation, only that organisation's own admins are notified.
- Admin accounts now also get a personal, non-dismissible notification whenever a two-factor code from their own authenticator app is submitted again after it already signed someone in - a genuine authenticator app never produces the same code twice, so this catches a code that may have been seen by someone else, distinct from an ordinary wrong guess. Same as the account's other mandatory alerts, this one can't be turned off, and it does not count toward the existing repeated-failed-two-factor-attempts alert, since replaying a leaked code is a different kind of event than random guessing.
- The production container image now runs `apt-get upgrade` when installing its base packages, picking up Debian's own bookworm-security point-fixes (e.g. CVE-2026-86145, a high-severity libpcre2-8-0 issue Docker Scout flagged in the v0.6.8 image) instead of shipping whatever version the base image tag happened to bake in until its own next rebuild.
- Every database query now has a 30-second Postgres `statement_timeout` by default - previously nothing bounded how long an in-flight query could run once it reached the database (only connection acquisition had a timeout), so a query stuck behind a lock during a burst of writes could hang indefinitely instead of failing fast. The handful of deploy-time backfill scripts that intentionally run one long-running statement over an entire table use a separate, longer timeout instead, matching the external bound the deploy entrypoint already gives them. The worker's two dedicated Postgres connections (advisory-lock coordination and job-wake `LISTEN`) get the same 30-second bound, since they connect directly and never went through the timeout above.
- Bumped two transitive dependencies carrying newly-disclosed high-severity advisories: `js-yaml` (GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh, unbounded CPU use parsing certain YAML) and `svgo` (GHSA-w27v-7q3p-w38r and GHSA-4vpr-x523-8j87, `removeScripts` incompletely sanitizing SVG content) - both pulled in via the mail template renderer's `mjml`/`htmlnano` pipeline, `svgo` also via the admin icon-font build tooling. Also bumped `hono` to pick up a moderate-severity fix (GHSA-gqvv-2mrq-wpjv, GHSA-g6gw-c38x-mqfc, GHSA-crvj-82cr-hjcx) while addressing the others. No code changes - all three stayed within their already-declared version ranges.

---

### Deploy
- Container image: `ghcr.io/solarssk/admitto:0.7.0` (rolling `:0.7`)
- Migrations apply **automatically on container start**. **No manual `migrate deploy`.** Back up the database yourself before upgrading (the stack no longer takes an automatic pre-migration backup).
